tour.intro: This quick orientation answers where to go next. Detailed editing and prompting techniques can be learned from the videos.
tour.editorDescription: This is the day-to-day editing view once media is inside the project.
tour.editor1: Assets panel: import videos, audio, and images, then drag them to the timeline.
tour.editor2: Preview: review media and send a frame to Generate as a starting keyframe.
tour.editor3: Timeline: trim, ripple, snap, markers, and arrange your cut.
tour.editor4: Inspector: transform, crop, timing, effects, text, and adjustments for the selected item.
tour.generateDescription: Create images, videos, or audio with local or cloud workflows.
tour.generate1: Single mode is for one-off image, video, or audio jobs.
tour.generate2: Director mode walks through Setup, Script, Keyframes, and Videos.
tour.generate3: If a workflow is missing models or nodes, use Re-check before you queue anything.
tour.stockDescription: Search Pexels and import footage or stills directly into the current project.
tour.stock1: Best used when you need quick placeholder footage, inspiration, or background plates.
tour.stock2: Requires a Pexels API key in Settings.
tour.exportDescription: Render the current timeline to a deliverable file and manage the export queue.
tour.export1: Choose format, codec, render range, resolution, FPS, and audio settings.
tour.export2: Queue multiple exports if you want a few output variants.
tour.settingsDescription: Return here whenever the machine-specific setup changes.
tour.settings1: Projects folder, ComfyUI port, Comfy account API key, Pexels key, and new-project defaults all live here.
tour.settings2: If something works on one machine and not another, this is the first place to compare.

gettingStarted.footer: This in-app guide covers the essentials. See the videos for detailed editing and prompting techniques.

comfyGate.launcherLater: You can set or change the launcher later in Settings.

projectsFolder.missing: No projects folder is chosen yet. Projects and imported media need a home.
projectsFolder.gone: The projects folder {{path}} no longer exists. Choose it again or pick a new one.
projectsFolder.readOnly: Drama Studio cannot save into {{path}}. Pick a folder you can write to.

projectsFolder.ready: Projects folder is writable, with {{free}} free.

binary.missing: {{name}} is missing, so import, export and audio tools will not work. Reinstall Drama Studio to restore it.
binary.broken: {{name}} is present but did not run ({{error}}). Antivirus software sometimes blocks it; reinstall Drama Studio or allow it.

gpu.ready: GPU acceleration is on for preview and video decoding.
gpu.readyNoDecode: GPU acceleration is on. Hardware video decoding is off, so heavy footage may play back slower.
gpu.software: Preview is running without GPU acceleration, so playback will be slow. Update your graphics driver and restart Drama Studio.
gpu.unknown: GPU status could not be read.

captions.unsupported: On-device captions are not available on this platform yet.
captions.noEngine: The caption engine is not installed yet. It downloads once (about 150 MB) and then works offline.
captions.noModel: The caption engine is installed but has no speech model yet.
captions.ready: Caption engine ready with {{count}} speech model(s).

comfy.offline: Local ComfyUI is not reachable at {{endpoint}}, and no cloud key is saved, so generation is unavailable. Start ComfyUI or add a cloud key.
comfy.cloudOnly: Cloud only: you started without ComfyUI. Editing, captions and export work; set ComfyUI up when you want AI images, video or music.
comfy.offlineCloudOk: Local ComfyUI is not running at {{endpoint}}. Cloud workflows still work with your saved key.
comfy.offlineUseCloud: Local ComfyUI is not reachable at {{endpoint}}, and this PC is not a good fit for local video generation. Add a Comfy.org cloud key to generate shots in the cloud.

cloudKey.ready: Comfy.org cloud key saved. Cloud workflows are available.
cloudKey.missing: No Comfy.org cloud key. Add one to generate without a local GPU.

bridge.ready: The ComfyUI bridge is installed, so you can send results from ComfyUI straight to Drama Studio.
bridge.missing: The ComfyUI bridge is not installed. It adds a Send to Drama Studio button inside ComfyUI.

launcher.ready: ComfyUI launcher is set up, so Drama Studio can start and stop ComfyUI for you.
launcher.missing: No ComfyUI launcher is set. Point Drama Studio at your start script to start ComfyUI with one click.

pexels.ready: Pexels key saved. Stock search is available.
pexels.missing: Add a free Pexels API key to search stock footage and photos.

opticalFlow.ready: Frame interpolation runtime is installed for smooth slow motion.
opticalFlow.missing: The frame interpolation runtime is missing, so smooth slow motion is off. Reinstalling Drama Studio restores it.

rtx.ready: NVIDIA RTX upscaling runtime is installed.
rtx.missing: NVIDIA RTX upscaling is not installed. It is offered the first time you use RTX upscale on a clip.

mcp.stopped: Agent control (MCP) is not running. Only needed if you use AI agents with Drama Studio.

hardware.summaryNoGpu: {{cpu}} ({{cores}} threads), {{ram}} RAM. No dedicated graphics card was detected.
hardware.unknown: Hardware details could not be read.

ai.cloudWhy: Why cloud? Cloud models run on data-center GPUs, so they are fast and capable on any computer. The trade-offs: they need an internet connection, usually cost per use, and your prompts and media are sent to the provider you choose.

local-llm.good: Local AI assistant: this PC can run mid-size models (roughly 7–14B) locally with Ollama or LM Studio. Free, private and offline.
local-llm.limited: Local AI assistant: possible with small models (roughly 3–8B), but expect slower replies and less reliable multi-step edits. A cloud model is the better default.
local-llm.cloud: Local AI assistant: not recommended on this PC. Use a cloud model (Claude, OpenAI or DeepSeek) for the assistant.
local-llm.unknown: Local AI assistant: hardware could not be read, so local capability is unknown.

local-image.good: Local image generation: comfortable on this PC with ComfyUI.
local-image.limited: Local image generation: works with lighter models and lower resolutions; large models will be slow or fail.
local-image.cloud: Local image generation: not recommended on this PC. Use cloud workflows.
local-image.unknown: Local image generation: hardware could not be read.

local-video.good: Local video generation: this PC can run local video models in ComfyUI.
local-video.limited: Local video generation: possible with smaller or quantized video models, short clips and long waits.
local-video.cloud: Local video generation: not recommended on this PC. Use cloud workflows for video shots.
local-video.unknown: Local video generation: hardware could not be read.

reasons.vram: Your {{gpu}} has {{vram}} of video memory. An AI model must fit there to run at a usable speed; whatever does not fit spills into system RAM and runs many times slower.
reasons.unifiedMemory: Your Mac shares {{ram}} of memory between the system and the GPU. Roughly 70% of it is usable for AI models.
reasons.noGpu: No dedicated graphics card with enough memory was found, so AI models would run on the CPU, which is far too slow for interactive use.
reasons.lowRam: This PC has {{ram}} of RAM. Local AI needs at least 16 GB alongside the app, your footage and the operating system.
reasons.smallModels: The models that fit are small. They handle simple requests but often lose track of multi-step timeline edits and tool calls.
reasons.tooSmallForLlm: That is not enough for a model that can reliably understand and carry out editing instructions.
reasons.imageLimited: Newer image models need 12 GB or more; on {{vram}} you will need lighter or quantized versions.
reasons.videoLimited: Video models are the heaviest AI workload. On {{vram}} you will need quantized models, short clips and patience.
reasons.tooSmallForVideo: Current video models typically need 12–24 GB of video memory, so they would fail or take a very long time per shot here.
reasons.noCuda: Most local video and image workflows are built for NVIDIA CUDA GPUs. {{vendor}} GPUs often lack support or run much slower.

castLocker.title: Cast & Wardrobe Locker
castLocker.intro: Keep each character's face consistent across shots while their outfits change between scenes.
castLocker.noProject: Open a project to manage its cast.
castLocker.empty: No cast yet. Add a character, give them face photos from up to three angles, then add outfits. Generations and Short Film keyframes will keep their identity locked.
castLocker.name: Name
castLocker.identityPlaceholder: Face, hair and age only, e.g. late 30s, dark curly hair, freckles. Put clothing in an outfit instead.

anchors.title: Face anchors
anchors.help: Use head-and-shoulders crops with no costume in frame. Each shot uses the anchor closest to its camera angle.

crop.title: Crop the face anchor
crop.help: Drag the square over the head and shoulders. Leave clothing and background out so outfits can change freely.

wardrobe.title: Wardrobe
wardrobe.help: Outfits are kept separate from the face, so changing one never changes who the character looks like. Add keywords, an outfit photo (headless or flat-lay works best), or both.
wardrobe.keywordsPlaceholder: Costume keywords, e.g. long beige trench coat, grey fedora

lock.help: Lock this character onto new image and video generations in this project.

tags.title: Tag selected clips
tags.selectClips: Select clips on the timeline to tag which cast members appear in them.
tags.help: Tagging {{count}} selected clip(s). Tags record who appears and in which outfit.

castLocker.consent: Face photos are sent to whichever model runs a generation, including cloud providers. Only use photos of people who have agreed to it.

button.label: Cast
button.title: Open the Cast & Wardrobe Locker
button.lockedTitle: {{name}} is locked onto new generations. Click to manage the cast.

projectDialog.resolutionIntro: Pick the shape that matches where your video will be posted.
projectDialog.frameRateIntro: Not sure? 24 gives a film look; 30 suits most online video.

resolution.hd720: Smaller, faster HD for drafts or YouTube
resolution.custom: Type your own width and height

fps.f25: TV standard in Europe and other PAL regions
fps.f30: Most online video and social media
fps.f60: Smooth motion for gaming and sports

format.mp4: Plays almost everywhere. Best for YouTube, social and sharing.
format.webm: Small web video. Some phones and editors can't open it.
format.prores: Very large, high-quality master for other editing apps.
format.audio: Sound only, no picture: music, voice-over or podcasts.
format.pngSeq: One image per frame, for VFX and compositing apps.
format.gif: Short, silent looping clip for chats and web pages.

videoCodec.h264: Most compatible. Choose this if you're unsure.
videoCodec.h265: Smaller files at the same quality; some older devices can't play it.
videoCodec.vp9: Open web codec used by WebM.

qualityMode.crf: Keeps quality steady while file size varies. Best for most people.
qualityMode.bitrate: Caps the data rate, for platforms with a size limit.

export.crf: Lower number = better quality and a bigger file. 18–23 looks great.
export.bitrate: Higher = better quality and a bigger file. 8,000–12,000 kbps suits 1080p.

preset.fast: Encodes faster; the file is a bit larger.
preset.medium: A good balance of speed and file size.
preset.slow: Takes longer for a slightly smaller file at the same quality.

keyframeMode.auto: Let the encoder decide. Right for nearly everyone.
keyframeMode.manual: Force a keyframe every N frames, for platforms that ask for it.

export.keyframeInterval: One keyframe every 2 seconds (48 at 24 fps) suits most streaming sites.

resolution.scaled: Smaller size for a quick test export.

audioCodec.aac: Standard audio for MP4. Plays everywhere.
audioCodec.mp3: Small and plays everywhere, with slight quality loss.

audioSampleRate.r48: Video standard. Best for most video work.

audioChannels.stereo: Left and right speakers. Best for most video.
audioChannels.mono: One channel. Fine for voice-only recordings.

settings.projectDefaults: New projects start with these choices. You can still change them in the New Project window.

generate.duration: Longer clips take more time to generate and may use more credits.
generate.seed: Same seed + same prompt = same result. Change it for a new variation.
generate.randomizeSeed: Pick a random seed for a new variation
generate.interpolation: Adds in-between frames for smoother motion. Higher is smoother but slower.

inspector.blendMode: How this clip mixes with the layers below. Normal: no mixing. Screen or Lighten: brightens (light leaks, glows). Multiply: darkens (shadows, textures).
inspector.trackMatte: Uses the clip above as a stencil, so this clip only shows through that clip's shape (Alpha) or brightness (Luma).
inspector.speed: 1× is normal speed. Below 1× is slow motion; above 1× speeds it up.

model.base: Fastest, smallest download. Good for clear speech.
model.small: More accurate with accents and noisy audio. Medium download.
model.best: Most accurate. Largest download; recommended if you have the space.

ducking.reductionDb: How much quieter the music gets while someone talks.
ducking.attackMs: How quickly the music dips when speech starts.
ducking.holdMs: How long the music stays low during short pauses.
ducking.releaseMs: How quickly the music comes back up afterwards.
ducking.thresholdDb: How loud speech must be to duck the music. Lower catches quieter voices.
ducking.detector: RMS is smoother and right for most dialogue.

comfyRequired.title: {{feature}} needs ComfyUI
comfyRequired.body: {{feature}} runs through ComfyUI, the free AI engine. You chose to start without it, so it is not set up yet.

packImport.title: Import pack
packImport.intro: Load the workflows, prompts and media that creators share as a .zip. You choose what to keep. Code in a pack is never run.
packImport.pickHelp: Choose a .zip or .dspack. Drama Studio opens it in a temporary folder, checks every file, and shows you what is inside before anything is kept.
packImport.reading: Opening the pack and checking every file…

sections.templatesHint: Kept with the pack and its read-me in the Drama Studio data folder.
sections.mediaHint: Images, audio and video go to Assets › {{pack}}. LUTs go to your LUT library (Inspector › Color).
sections.mediaNeedsProject: Open a project to import images, audio and video. LUTs can be imported now.
sections.codeHint: Drama Studio does not run or install code from packs. None of these files were saved.

check.ready: Ready: your ComfyUI has every node this uses.
check.offline: ComfyUI is not connected, so nodes were not checked yet.
check.fixHint: You can still import it. Open it from My Workflows: ComfyUI Manager offers to install missing nodes, and Workflow Setup downloads models.

codeType.chrome-extension: This is a Chrome extension. Drama Studio does not run extensions from packs.
codeType.script: These are scripts. Drama Studio does not run scripts from packs.
codeType.windows-script: These are Windows scripts (.bat, .ps1…). They can change your computer, so Drama Studio does not run them.
codeType.python: This is Python code, often a ComfyUI custom node. Install custom nodes through ComfyUI Manager, not from a pack.
codeType.program: These are programs. Drama Studio never runs programs from packs.
codeType.installer: These are installers. Drama Studio never installs software from packs.
codeType.extension-package: This is a packaged browser extension. Drama Studio does not install extensions.
codeType.web-page: These are web pages that can run scripts. Drama Studio does not open them.

pattern.long-video: It looks like a tool that chains clips into a long video. Drama Studio does that built in: Generate › Short Film Creation plans shot after shot, and right-click a clip › Continue from last frame extends a shot.
pattern.limit-bypass: It says it gets around the limits of a service. Drama Studio will not use it, and using it can get your account banned.
pattern.automation: It automates clicks on a website. In Drama Studio the generation queue runs batches for you.

skipReason.archive: a pack inside the pack, not opened
skipReason.model: model file; get models through Workflow Setup

done.title: Pack imported
done.luts: LUTs added to the LUT library: {{count}}

errors.UNSAFE_PATH: This pack has a file that tries to write outside its folder. Drama Studio will not open it.
errors.ZIP_BOMB: This pack unpacks to far more than its size says (it may be a zip bomb). Drama Studio will not open it.
errors.TOO_MANY_FILES: This pack has too many files to import (more than 5,000).
errors.TOO_BIG: This pack unpacks to more than 2 GB. Ask for a smaller pack, or split it.
errors.NOT_ZIP: This is not a .zip or .dspack that Drama Studio can open.
errors.NOT_FOUND: That file could not be found.
errors.EMPTY: Nothing in this pack can be imported: no workflows, prompts or media.
errors.EXPIRED: This pack is no longer open. Open it again.
errors.desktopOnly: Importing packs is only available in the desktop app.

packImport.browserButtonTitle: Load workflows, prompts and media from a .zip a creator shared
packImport.browserEmptyHint: Got a pack from another creator? Use Import pack… or drop the .zip here.
